title: 4. Prepositions & Dependency Rules
group: Module 1 · The Foundational Zero-to-Hero Grammar Engine
blocks: Prepositions of time, place, and direction, the Task 1 data prepositions, dependent prepositions to memorise in blocks, and the direct-translation errors that mark a script as Bangladeshi.

Prepositions are the small words (in, on, at, by, for, to, of, from, with) that show how other words relate in time, place, and direction. They look trivial, but they carry a large share of the errors on this test, for one reason: prepositions are memorised by pattern, not by logic. There is no rule that explains why English says interested in but good at and afraid of. These are fixed collocations, and they either sound right to a native ear or they do not. For a Bangla speaker, that is a problem, because your instinct is to translate the Bangla preposition directly, and Bangla maps its relationships differently.

A preposition sits before a noun or pronoun and shows a relationship: the book is on the table (place), the meeting is at three (time), she walked into the room (direction). The noun after it is called its object. One key rule you already met in the tenses chapter returns here: after a preposition, a verb always takes the -ing form, never the infinitive. Interested in studying, responsible for managing, capable of solving.
4.2 Prepositions of time · in, on, at, and their neighbours
The three core time prepositions follow a “zooming in” logic, from long periods to exact points.
months, years, seasons, centuries, long periods
in July, in 2020, in winter, in the 1990s
on Monday, on 5 May, on weekdays
at 5 p.m., at night, at the weekend, at the start
Other time prepositions that matter for IELTS:
since + a starting point (goes with the present perfect): since 2010, since January.
for + a length of time: for five years, for a decade.
during + a period (when something happens within it): during the 1990s, during the recession.
by + a deadline (not later than): by 2030, by the end of the decade.
from … to / until + a span: from 2000 to 2010, until 2015.
In Monday the shop is closed. / The population grew since five years.
On Monday the shop is closed. / The population grew for five years.
in = inside a space or area: in the room, in Dhaka, in the world.
on = on a surface or line: on the wall, on the coast, on the second floor.
at = at a specific point or place: at the station, at the top, at home.
into / onto / to show movement or direction: walk into the room, climb onto the roof, go to work.
The figures are shown in the chart, on the vertical axis, at the top of the page.
4.4 The Task 1 data prepositions (memorise as fixed phrases)
These combinations describe movement and quantity on a graph. They are non-negotiable in Writing Task 1, and examiners expect every one of them to be exact.
a range or a time span
Sales increased with 20 per cent and reached to a peak in June.
Sales increased by 20 per cent and reached a peak in June.
“increase by” a percentage; “reach a peak” takes no preposition after “reach.”
A single strong Task 1 sentence often chains several of these: The price rose by five dollars, from 20 to 25, reaching a peak of 25 in March.
4.5 Dependent prepositions (the ones after specific words)
Many verbs, adjectives, and nouns are followed by a fixed preposition. There is no logic; you learn each as a unit. Memorise them in blocks and use them until they feel automatic.
The policy resulted in higher costs.
The panel consists of five experts.
The essay focuses on two causes.
Families struggle to cope with rising costs.
Individuals are responsible for their choices.
People are more aware of the risks.
The system is capable of handling demand.
This trend is similar to the previous one.
Urban life is different from rural life.
He is good at solving problems.
The economy is dependent on exports.
The issue is related to poverty.
The course is suitable for beginners.

These are the specific errors that come from translating a Bangla structure word for word. They are extremely common and instantly recognisable to an examiner, so fixing them gives a fast, visible accuracy gain.

discuss / enter / reach / marry take a direct object — no preposition
✗ discuss about the topic / enter into the room / reach to the destination / marry with her
✓ discuss the topic / enter the room / reach the destination / marry her

according to me / return back / comprise of / mention about / cope up with
✗ According to me / return back home / comprise of three parts / mention about it / cope up with
✓ In my opinion / return home / comprise three parts / mention it / cope with

Prepositions affect your score in two visible places. In Writing Task 1, the data prepositions (by, from, to, of, at) are so standard that getting one wrong stands out immediately as an accuracy error. In Writing Task 2 and Speaking, the dependent prepositions (depend on, lead to, responsible for, solution to) and the direct-translation errors (discuss about, according to me) separate controlled from uncontrolled English. Because these are collocations, correct ones also lift your Lexical Resource score, so the payoff is double.

Skills: Writing, Speaking
Task 1: Unemployment rose by four points, from six to ten per cent, before falling to eight in 2015.
Task 2: A lack of investment in public transport contributes to congestion and leads to higher emissions.
Speaking Part 3: It really depends on the situation, but on balance I think education is the solution to most of these problems.
End of Chapter 4, and of Module 1. Module 2 (Band 7.0+ Complex Structures), Chapter 5 follows.

title: 4. Practice · Prepositions & Dependency Rules
group: Module 1 · The Foundational Zero-to-Hero Grammar Engine
blocks: Many verbs, adjectives, and nouns are locked to a specific preposition with no logic behind the pairing -- you simply have to memorise each one as a fixed unit: depend ON, responsible FOR, an increase IN.
**Why it matters:** Dependent prepositions are pure memorisation, but they're everywhere in academic writing, and getting them wrong reads as a basic error even in an otherwise strong sentence.
Learn them in blocks, by word type
**Verb + preposition:** depend on, lead to, result in, result from.
**Adjective + preposition:** responsible for, interested in, aware of, capable of.
**Noun + preposition:** an increase/rise in, a reason for, a solution to, an effect/impact on.
There's no shortcut here -- memorise each pairing as a single chunk, not as two separate words, and practise them inside full sentences until the pairing feels automatic rather than looked-up.

blocks.title: Exercise 4.1 · Preposition Fill-in
blocks.instructions: Fill each gap with the correct preposition. Some gaps take no preposition; write (0) for those.

items.prompt: The number of tourists rose ______ 20 per cent last year.
The figure grew ______ 5 million ______ 8 million ______ 2015.
Air pollution largely results ______ vehicle emissions.
The government should invest more ______ renewable energy.
She is very interested ______ studying abroad.
Rapid urbanisation has led ______ a housing shortage.
Unemployment peaked ______ 12 per cent ______ 2009.
The success of the plan depends ______ adequate funding.
Many students suffer ______ a lack ______ confidence.
He is responsible ______ managing the entire department.
This problem is closely related ______ poverty.
We must discuss ______ the main causes of the issue.
items.reason: “discuss” takes a direct object, no preposition.

items.prompt: There has been a sharp increase ______ demand ______ housing.
The committee consists ______ seven members.
The shop is closed ______ Fridays but open ______ the weekend.
Consumption fell ______ a low ______ five units in 2012.
Cities in the region rely heavily ______ agriculture.
The report focuses ______ the effects ______ climate change.
Please enter ______ the hall quietly. (direct object verb)
The two graphs are similar ______ each other.
Students benefit greatly ______ regular feedback.
She applied ______ a scholarship ______ a British university.
A good education is the solution ______ many social problems.
The population has been rising steadily ______ 2000.
items.reason: “since 2000” (a starting point, with the present perfect).

items.prompt: According ______ the chart, spending increased sharply.
items.reason: “according to the chart” (a source, which is correct here).

blocks: A preposition shows a relationship -- place, time, or direction -- and its object follows it. When your English feels subtly wrong, check whether you've translated a Bangla preposition pattern directly instead of using the fixed English one.
**Why it matters:** Most preposition errors from Bangla speakers come from translating the L1 pattern word-for-word rather than learning the English pairing as its own fixed unit.
A preposition sits before a noun or pronoun and shows a relationship: on the table (place), at three (time), into the room (direction). The noun that follows is called its object.

Whenever a preposition feels uncertain, resist translating from Bangla directly. Instead, recall the fixed English phrase as a whole chunk -- depend on, not "depend from" or "depend of" -- since English prepositions rarely map one-to-one onto their Bangla equivalents.

blocks.title: Exercise 4.2 · L1 Direct-Translation Fix
blocks.instructions: Each sentence contains a preposition error caused by direct translation from Bangla. Rewrite each one correctly.

items.prompt: According to me, the government should act quickly.
items.answer: In my opinion, the government should act quickly.
accepted: In my opinion, the government should act quickly.
items.reason: “according to me” is wrong for your own view.

items.prompt: We discussed about the new policy for an hour.
items.answer: We discussed the new policy for an hour.
accepted: We discussed the new policy for an hour.

items.prompt: He entered into the classroom without knocking.
items.answer: He entered the classroom without knocking.
accepted: He entered the classroom without knocking.

items.prompt: The teacher emphasised on the importance of grammar.
items.answer: The teacher emphasised the importance of grammar.
accepted: The teacher emphasised the importance of grammar.

items.prompt: After the trip, they returned back to their village.
items.answer: After the trip, they returned to their village.
accepted: After the trip, they returned to their village.
items.reason: “return” already means “go back,” so “back” is redundant.

items.prompt: The report comprises of five main sections.
items.answer: The report comprises five main sections.
accepted: The report comprises five main sections.

items.prompt: She married with a doctor last year.
items.answer: She married a doctor last year.
accepted: She married a doctor last year.

items.prompt: I want to request to you for some help.
items.answer: I want to ask you for some help.
accepted: I want to ask you for some help.
I want to make a request to you for some help.

items.prompt: The essay mentioned about three possible solutions.
items.answer: The essay mentioned three possible solutions.
accepted: The essay mentioned three possible solutions.

items.prompt: The researchers investigated about the causes of pollution.
items.answer: The researchers investigated the causes of pollution.
accepted: The researchers investigated the causes of pollution.

items.prompt: We must cope up with the rising cost of living.
items.answer: We must cope with the rising cost of living.
accepted: We must cope with the rising cost of living.

items.prompt: The minister reached to the venue an hour late.
items.answer: The minister reached the venue an hour late.
accepted: The minister reached the venue an hour late.

items.prompt: My opinion is different than yours on this matter.
items.answer: My opinion is different from yours on this matter.
accepted: My opinion is different from yours on this matter.
items.reason: “different from” is the standard academic form.

items.prompt: Students should concentrate in their studies.
items.answer: Students should concentrate on their studies.
accepted: Students should concentrate on their studies.

items.prompt: The country is suffering with severe traffic congestion.
items.answer: The country is suffering from severe traffic congestion.
accepted: The country is suffering from severe traffic congestion.
